text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: canary 'eu-small' error-rate > 5% (5m). Latency up, 5xx spike. Paging oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-failure

sre-ellie: On it. grabbing context. Which release?

priya: Release tag: release-2026-03-17-eu. Rolled canary to 10% 3m ago. I see increased 502s from model-proxy in logs.

ops-nate: Noticed traffic shaping rule for route_v2 changed labels, possibly misrouted requests -> backend mismatch.

eng-james: quick tail of proxy logs: `2026-03-17T16:07:20Z proxy eu-small 502 upstream-unexpected-response` repeated. Also memory pressure on a subset of inference nodes.

incident-bot: auto-rollback attempt: failed. Reason: precondition-migration-lock preventing pipeline rollback. See /ci/rollout/1234 -> status: blocked

sre-ellie: Ok, automated rollback blocked. Plan A: flip feature flag route_v2 -> off (kill-switch) to stop new canary traffic and drain. Plan B: if flag toggle fails, manual traffic-rewrite to pin to stable. Priya, can you flip and confirm? Ops-nate, prepare drain commands. Maria, heads-up to CS for possible customer-facing note.

priya: toggling flag now via admin api. Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://flags.redwood.internal/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"route_v2","state":"off","actor":"priya"}'
```

priya: flag toggle returned 200. UI shows route_v2=OFF. :white_check_mark:

ops-nate: Starting gradual drain of canary pool to 0% over 90s using traffic-shaper:
```
traffic-shaper --pool eu-small --set-weight 10% --step 5% --interval 15s --target 0%
```

ops-nate: Drain in progress. Observability -> canary traffic 10% -> 6% -> 2%

eng-james: Monitoring error-rate after flag flip: 5xx dropping. Last 1m error-rate 1.2% (was 6.8%). Memory pressure easing on nodes that were hot.

priya: Because auto-rollback blocked, I'll kick manual rollback of the canary image tag to stable-pinned across EU after drain completes. Running rollout command now:
```
redwoodctl rollout set --env eu --service inference --tag stable-pinned --force --reason "canary spike" --actor priya
```

deploy-bot: Rollout job 5872 queued -> started. Logs: pulling stable-pinned, draining old pods, applying config.

maria-cs: Customer-impact check: we surfaced a handful of 502s for a small % of EU sessions (estimated <0.4% of total requests). Preparing a proactive note for top 25 accounts; will wait for final confirmation.

sre-ellie: Running smoke checks once drain hits 0 and rollout reaches healthy. Smoke checklist:
- curl https://api.eu.redwood.ai/health (expect 200)
- 10 synthetic inference calls (expect <=200ms p50, <=500ms p95)
- check tracing for error-rate regressions

ops-nate: Drain at 0% now. Old canary instances are in Evicting state.

deploy-bot: Rollout job 5872 complete. Canary tag replaced with stable-pinned. Instances: 12/12 healthy.

sre-ellie: Running smoke now:
`curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://api.eu.redwood.ai/health` -> 200
Synthetic runs: 10/10 success, p50 180ms p95 360ms. Traces show normal tails.

eng-james: Confirming logs: no 502 spikes in last 10m. Latency normalized.

maria-cs: Draft sent to top accounts summarizing: small fraction saw 502s during a canary rollout; we reverted canary and service is healthy. Asking for review.

sre-ellie: Good. Closing actions:
- create incident ticket with timeline + root-cause hypothesis: mislabel in traffic config caused mismatched backend -> proxy 502s + memory pressure on subset
- follow-up: unblock CI precondition for auto-rollback (migration-lock check) to avoid manual step next time
- engineering to add a pre-rollout sanity check for proxy-backend contract

priya: Filing PR for guard in deploy pipeline to validate route labels match backend config.

ops-nate: Noted. I'll add a short runbook snippet for emergency drain commands.

incident-bot: Incident archived as severity: Sev2. Duration: ~28m. Pager handoff: oncall -> next. Tags: canary, rollback, feature-flag.

sre-ellie: Closing the thread. :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone.

eng-james: +1 good job.

maria-cs: Sending customer comms now.
